text.p: Leading political parties on Tuesday wrapped up talks on the new government declaration and coalition agreement, which they are to publicly present on Wednesday.

"This declaration has very concrete terms of implementation. The declaration focuses on the two most important things: integration with European structures and the continuation of reforms," Prime Minister-candidate Guntar Krasts told Reuters.
The declaration, which sets out the new government's aims and proposals, is expected to differ little from that of outgoing premier, Andris Shkele.
The coalition agreement also foresees that members of parliament from outside the coalition parties can be invited to be cabinet ministers.
The declaration is also likely to say that a balanced budget is desirable this year but may be more realistic for next year, politicians said.
Parliament's vote to confirm the new government in office is expected to take place on August 7, the politicians added.
